# Mobile apps

Applies when the change touches: iOS, Android, cross-platform. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Standards

| Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OWASP MASVS and MASTG | MASVS 2.1, MASTG v2 | 2026-09-28 | <https://mas.owasp.org/> |
| Apple Human Interface Guidelines and App Review Guidelines | current | 2026-09-28 | <https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/> |
| Material Design and Google Play policy | Material Design 3; Material 3, policy current | 2026-09-28 | <https://m3.material.io/foundations> |
| Platform privacy manifests and data-safety declarations | current | 2026-09-28 | <https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469> |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | A store-facing change (permissions, data collection, payments, sign-in) is major: platform review policy is a dependency. |
| Specify | Every permission and data use in the Spec with its purpose string; the privacy manifest and data-safety changes planned as a Task. |
| Specify | Offline, background, interruption, and low-battery states in the Acceptance. |
| Implement | Secrets in the keystore or keychain, never in the bundle; certificate pinning where MASVS requires; no sensitive data in logs or screenshots. |
| Review | The MASVS controls for the change's category (storage, crypto, auth, network, platform, code, resilience). |
| Ship | Staged rollout with crash-free rate and ANR or hang rate as the rollback trigger; the store console metrics are the `[observe]` signals. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MobSF static scan | no high finding in the build | `mobsfscan` on the source, MobSF on the binary |
| MASTG test cases | the touched controls hold | the MASTG cases for the change's category, scripted where possible |
| UI tests on the OS matrix | the flows work on every supported OS version | XCUITest, Espresso, or Detox in CI |
| Accessibility scan (emerging) | labels, contrast, and touch targets pass | Accessibility Inspector and Android Accessibility Scanner |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
